newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore oil products unchanged in quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: Singapore oil products unchanged in quiet trade.

text.p: Singapore oil products were largely unchanged in quiet trading due to holiday in Japan and no fresh news from the MidEast, traders said on Monday.
Gas oil swaps firmed but physical prices were lagging due to thin buying interest. October swaps firmed to $27.60-27.75, up from Friday's close of $27.35-27.45, brokers said.
Gas oil remained firm as supplies from South Korean for loading in October were expected to be half of the 8-10 cargoes sold in September, industry sources said.
Traders said they estimated South Korea would have between three and five cargoes for export in October.

South Korea sellers offered the 0.5 percent sulphur gas oil at 30-40 cents premium on a fob basis. They have already sold several 0.1 percent cargoes about $1.00 per barrel premium on a fob South Korea basis, traders said.
In Singapore, a trader was bidding for 150,000 barrels loading on Oct 13-17 at $27.55 fob against an offer from a major at $27.95, brokers said.

Jet picked up slightly as buyers returned to the market. Offer by a U.S trader for a 100,000 barrel cargo loading on Oct 11-15 at 29.60 was sold to a Mediterrenean trader. October gas oil/jet spread was quoted at $2.55-2.70.
Light distillates were also steady. Naphtha swaps for October were talked at $20.80/$21.00, up 10 cents from Friday.

Gasoline was quiet ahead of Taiwan's import tender for reformate which closes on Tuesday. Talks for 95-octane unleaded grade was limited to just a bid heard at Friday's last deal level of $22.60 per barrrel fob Singapore for October 19-23.
A deal was heard done for the same timing for 50,000 barrels of 92-octane at $22.10.
Fuel oil remained steady amid firm fundamentals. Traders said China is still a buyer for October barrels.
